title: AI Automation Consultant
description: We build and run software that schedules work crews, texts them their jobs, and handles what they get paid. It runs live every day for real businesses. If it breaks, real people don't get told where to go, and real money goes to the wrong place. An AI writes most of the code. We need someone to decide what gets built, and to catch the AI when it gets it wrong -- because it does, and it always sounds confident. What we pay $1,000 a month to start. We review it after your first few weeks, and again once you've shown what you can do. The step up from this job is Client Lead -- you'd run a client on your own and be the person they talk to. It pays significantly more, and we fill it by promoting someone who's already doing this job well. That's where this role is meant to lead. What you'll do Take a vague complaint -- "the schedule is wrong sometimes" -- and work out what's actually happening before changing anything. Write down what a new feature should do, and just as importantly what it should not do, before any code is written. Use the AI to build it, then check its work properly. Read the code like someone is trying to slip something past you. Test on real data with the feature switched off, then switch it on and watch. Nothing goes straight to texting a hundred people. When something breaks: stop the damage, find everything affected, then fix the cause -- not just the one thing that got reported. Write short, clear updates. Most days that's how your team knows what's going on. Who does well here You've built something real. One thing is enough. Something messy, that other people ended up depending on. We'd rather hear about that than a list of technologies. You don't take "it works" for an answer. A passing test and a green dashboard don't settle it for you. You go and check. You think about what happens when things go wrong -- bad input, the same job running twice, someone in a different timezone, a message that says "sent" but never arrived. You're fine saying "I don't know yet, here's how I'd find out." You don't need a degree, a particular language, or years of experience. You do need good judgment, and we test for that directly instead of guessing from your CV. This isn't for you if you want tickets handed to you with the thinking already done, or if you'd ship the AI's first answer because it looked right. How to apply https://volt-os-production-4bc9.up.railway.app/apply Fill in a short form, verify who you are with Telegram, and a 20-minute timed test starts straight away. Do it when you have twenty quiet minutes and decent internet -- you only get one go at it. In the form, tell us about one thing you built that mattered. What was unclear at the start, what you got wrong, and how you found out. That's the part we read closely. What happens after Timed test -- arithmetic, patterns, following written instructions (20 min) Written questions about real situations from the system (~2 hrs) A repo with a bad change hidden in it, and some unfamiliar code to get into (~4-5 hrs) A conversation -- real problems, out loud (~2 hrs) Paid trial, real work, everything reviewed (2-4 weeks) Steps 1-4 are unpaid. The trial is paid from your first day. Most people don't get past step 3. That's expected -- the whole job is about holding a high bar, so we'd rather find out early than three months in. If you need something changed to take this fairly -- extra time, a screen reader, a different format -- just tell us before you start. Asking costs you nothing and isn't part of the test.

title: Veterinary Nurse – Phlebotomist (South West)
description: Home About us Our people Join our team Veterinary Nurse – Phlebotomist (South West) Veterinary Nurse – Phlebotomist (South West) Part time (Minimum of 12 sessions a year) | Saturdays/Sundays | £15 p/hour Primarily on the West Coast (Cardiff, Gloucester, Bristol, Wellington, Wells) Closing date for applications: 10 August 2026 The Role Animal charity Pet Blood Bank UK are recruiting for the position of a Registered Veterinary Nurse to work as a phlebotomist at venues across the SW (primarily in the areas of Cardiff, Gloucester, Bristol, Wellington and Wells). As part of the collection team, this role involves working at donation sessions where lifesaving blood is collected from dogs. As a phlebotomist, you are responsible for performing blood collections from our canine donors, whilst working alongside the supervising Veterinary Surgeon and Donor Assistants. There is the potential to meet up to 23 donors and their owners at each session. The role is key to ensuring successful donation sessions and providing a positive experience for all our donors and their owners. A willingness to travel is essential as there may be times you are asked to work across the entire region, which spans from Somerset to Hampshire, Oxfordshire to South Wales and all areas in between! Background Launched in 2007, Pet Blood Bank UK is the only charity that provides a blood bank service for all vets across the UK. As part of our charitable remit, our aim is to advance animal health and welfare and to relieve suffering by providing quick and convenient access to blood. Every unit of blood helps save up to four other lives, saving thousands of lives every year. Our values Caring. Pioneering. Real. These are the values Pet Blood Bank UK is built upon. Our values bind us together as a charity and guide everything we do. We expect every team member to know, understand and embody our values, helping to build our reputation as a pioneering, caring and practical charity. Read more about our values. What you'll do Perform canine whole blood unit collections under direction of the supervising Veterinary Surgeon. Ensure donor records are completed correctly, accurately and in full, both on paper and electronically. Ensure donor owners are fully aware of the blood donation process. Build a rapport with donors and their owners to ensure they feel valued and involved - provide a positive donation experience from start to finish. Maintain a good relationship with our host venues. Communicate with Pet Blood Bank staff, including your regional collection team, Regional Coordinator, Area Supervisor and office staff. Supervise Donor Assistants working on session, understand their role and perform Donor Assistant tasks if required. Ensure donors are monitored both throughout the donation process and in post donation. Provide post donation communication to donor owners. Assist with and support the training of new team members and ensure all training records are completed correctly. Attend events to promote Pet Blood Bank and recruit donors and volunteers. What we need We're Looking For Someone Who Is Is a Registered Veterinary Nurse with a minimum of 2 years post registration clinical experience. An interest in phlebotomy and confidence to learn a new skill Confident working in a small team and the ability to lead/direct those working with you in donation Holds a full UK driving licence and has access to their own transport. Is organised, pro-active and team orientated. Has the ability to problem solve, has good organisation skills and attention to detail. Is an excellent communicator with strong customer care skills. Is confident in blood sampling with owners present. Availability on weekends. To ensure you can complete the required training we may arrange for you to attend some sessions outside of the region, mileage allowance and accommodation will be organised where required. What's in it for you In return, we offer full training and a great team working environment. The rate of pay is £15/hour and a mileage allowance of 35p/mile offered for travel to and from venues. Further Details Sessions are approximately 8 hours in length and flexibility is essential as start and finish times will be dependent upon the location of the venue. Pet Blood Bank envisage that you will work approximately 1 session a month, however there may be the option to work more. Own transport is required to get to venues - please note not all venues are accessible by public transport. Before applying, please read our Guidance for Candidates. For more information or to request a full job description, please email recruitment@petbloodbankuk.org. To apply, please complete our application form and email it to recruitment@petbloodbankuk.org.
